intent.raw_query: Costa Rica eco-adventure, $2500, zip-lining and wildlife, February 2026 from Miami

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits, featuring over 10 cables, Tarzan swings, and suspension bridges with breathtaking views of the forest below. A top eco-adventure experience with expert naturalist guides who point out wildlife along the way.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife River Safari
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle waterways of Tortuguero by canoe or small boat, spotting caimans, river turtles, howler monkeys, sloths, toucans, and vibrant poison dart frogs in their natural habitat. If visiting between July and October, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of endangered green sea turtles on the beach at night.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Wildlife Hike
experiences.description: Trek through primary rainforest on a network of hanging bridges and trails surrounding the iconic Arenal Volcano. Encounter toucans, morpho butterflies, coatis, and howler monkeys while crossing suspension bridges high above the forest floor with stunning volcano views. Guided tours include expert naturalist commentary.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Tour
experiences.description: Explore one of the world's most biodiverse national parks with a certified naturalist guide and high-powered telescope. Spot three-toed sloths, white-faced capuchin monkeys, scarlet macaws, and rare squirrel monkeys in the jungle, then relax on the park's stunning white-sand beaches framed by lush rainforest.

experiences.name: Corcovado National Park Day Trek with Naturalist Guide
experiences.description: Venture into one of the most biologically intense places on Earth, as described by National Geographic. This guided day hike through Corcovado's old-growth rainforest offers unparalleled chances to see tapirs, peccaries, scarlet macaws, poison dart frogs, and even jaguars. An unmissable bucket-list eco-adventure for serious wildlife enthusiasts.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Costa Rica
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, exchange currency or withdraw colones from ATM (better rates than airport exchange). Take the budget-friendly public bus or shared shuttle to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and explore the beachfront property and surrounding area on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Take a leisurely sunset walk along the beach adjacent to the resort. Get oriented with nearby streets, locate the closest sodas (local budget restaurants) and mini-markets for future reference.

meals.breakfast: Eat before or during the flight
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and affordable casado (rice, beans, meat, salad) at a local soda near the airport or bus terminal for around $5-7 USD
meals.dinner: Dinner at a beachside soda near the resort - try gallo pinto with grilled fish for approximately $7-10 USD

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light due to afternoon arrival. Prioritize rest and orientation. Avoid expensive resort dining tonight - explore local sodas instead. Keep $20-30 USD in small bills for tips and small purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a self-guided wildlife walk along the beach at sunrise (free). Look for howler monkeys, scarlet macaws, and iguanas in the trees near the resort. Bring water and wear light clothing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearest national park or wildlife reserve accessible from the beachfront area. Explore hiking trails independently without a guide to save money. Look for sloths, toucans, and coatis along the trail.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and browse the local artisan market or town center. Pick up snacks from a local pulpería (corner store) for budget-friendly refreshments.

meals.breakfast: Buy fresh fruit, bread, and instant coffee from a nearby pulpería for under $3 USD
meals.lunch: Pack a simple lunch from the pulpería - sandwiches, fruit, and water - to eat on the trail
meals.dinner: Casado at a local soda in town - rice, beans, plantains, and chicken for $6-8 USD

day_by_day.notes: February is dry season in most of Costa Rica, making it ideal for wildlife spotting. Bring insect repellent and sunscreen. Wear neutral-colored clothing to avoid disturbing wildlife.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning birdwatching walk along the beach and mangrove edges (free). Bring binoculars if available. February is excellent for spotting migratory birds. Look for herons, egrets, and kingfishers near any river mouths.
day_by_day.afternoon: Book a budget zip-lining tour through a local operator (avoid resort-booked tours which carry markups). Look for group rates or last-minute discounts at local tour offices. Budget zip-line tours typically cost $35-55 USD per person. Enjoy the canopy experience and aerial wildlife views.
day_by_day.evening: Relax on the beach and watch the sunset. Join any free beach volleyball or social activities happening near the resort.

meals.breakfast: Gallo pinto with egg and fresh juice at a local soda - traditional Costa Rican breakfast for $4-5 USD
meals.lunch: Light snack at the zip-line location or pack fruit and granola bars from the pulpería
meals.dinner: Try a local comida típica restaurant - order the plato del día (plate of the day) for $7-9 USD, usually includes soup, main course, and drink

day_by_day.notes: Book zip-lining directly with local operators rather than through the resort to save 20-40%. Ask about student or group discounts. Wear closed-toe shoes and avoid loose jewelry.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the local town or village near the resort on foot. Visit the central market or farmer's market if available on this day. Interact with locals and practice a few Spanish phrases - Costa Ricans (Ticos) are very welcoming.
day_by_day.afternoon: Self-guided snorkeling or swimming at the beach (free). Look for marine wildlife such as sea turtles, rays, and colorful fish in shallow reef areas. Rent basic snorkel gear locally if needed ($5-10 USD).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost cultural event in the nearby town if available. Otherwise, enjoy a bonfire or stargazing on the beach.

meals.breakfast: Fresh tropical fruit smoothie and empanadas from a street vendor for $3-4 USD
meals.lunch: Ceviche from a beachside shack - fresh, affordable, and delicious for $5-7 USD
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using ingredients from the local market if your accommodation has kitchen access, or eat at a budget soda for $6-8 USD

day_by_day.notes: Always negotiate or compare prices at local markets. Buying directly from vendors at the market is significantly cheaper than resort shops. Stay hydrated in the tropical heat.

day_by_day.morning: Take a public bus or shared shuttle to a nearby eco-adventure destination (waterfall, volcano viewpoint, or cloud forest edge depending on resort location). Public buses in Costa Rica are very affordable at $1-5 USD per trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike to a nearby waterfall or natural swimming hole. Many of these are free or have a minimal entrance fee of $2-5 USD. Swim in the natural pools and enjoy the lush jungle surroundings.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area by public bus. Rest and recover from the active day.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure - gallo pinto and eggs at a local soda near the bus stop for $4-5 USD
meals.lunch: Pack lunch from the pulpería to eat at the waterfall or natural attraction
meals.dinner: Treat yourself slightly - a slightly nicer local restaurant with fresh seafood for $12-15 USD as a mid-trip reward

day_by_day.notes: Check bus schedules the evening before. Carry exact change for public buses. Bring a waterproof bag for electronics near waterfalls. Start early to avoid afternoon heat.

day_by_day.morning: Join a free or low-cost guided nature walk offered by local conservation volunteers or community tourism initiatives. Many coastal communities in Costa Rica have free walking tours. Ask at the local tourism office.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding rental on the beach or in a nearby estuary. Look for budget rental shops away from the resort for better rates ($10-20 USD for 2 hours). Estuary kayaking offers excellent wildlife viewing.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the beachfront promenade or town square. Enjoy a fresh coconut water from a street vendor ($1-2 USD) and people-watch.

meals.breakfast: Bread, peanut butter, and banana from the pulpería - simple and budget-friendly at $2-3 USD
meals.lunch: Rice and beans with chicken at a local soda for $5-7 USD
meals.dinner: Street food night - try churros, patacones (fried plantains), or grilled corn from street vendors for $3-5 USD total

day_by_day.notes: Community-based tourism initiatives directly support local families and are often cheaper than commercial tours. Ask your hotel staff for recommendations on authentic local experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and leisure morning at the beach. Read, swim, or simply enjoy the tropical environment. Mid-trip rest day is important for maintaining energy for the second half of the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby wildlife rescue center or animal sanctuary. Many in Costa Rica charge a modest entrance fee of $10-20 USD and allow close encounters with sloths, monkeys, toucans, and other rescued animals.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset yoga on the beach (many hostels and community centers offer free or donation-based sessions). Alternatively, enjoy a quiet evening journaling or reviewing photos from the week.

meals.breakfast: Splurge slightly on a full breakfast at a local café - pancakes, fruit, and coffee for $6-8 USD
meals.lunch: Leftovers or snacks from the pulpería to keep costs low on the rest day
meals.dinner: Pizza or pasta at a budget international restaurant for variety - $8-12 USD

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is a mid-trip recharge day. Review your budget spending so far and adjust the second week accordingly. Check if any special wildlife events or guided night tours are available for upcoming days.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning guided bird tour with a local community guide (more affordable than agency tours at $15-25 USD). Costa Rica has over 900 bird species - February is excellent for sightings. Look for toucans, resplendent quetzals, and motmots.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby mangrove ecosystem by foot or kayak. Mangroves are free to explore on foot and are rich in wildlife including crocodiles, birds, and fish. Stay on marked paths for safety.
day_by_day.evening: Night wildlife walk - either self-guided along a lit trail or with a local guide ($15-20 USD). Spot nocturnal creatures like red-eyed tree frogs, night herons, and bats.

meals.breakfast: Eat before the early bird tour - quick gallo pinto and coffee at a soda for $3-4 USD
meals.lunch: Fresh fish tacos from a beachside vendor for $5-7 USD
meals.dinner: Arroz con pollo (rice with chicken) at a local soda for $6-8 USD

day_by_day.notes: For the night walk, bring a headlamp or flashlight. Wear long pants and closed shoes to protect against insects. Move slowly and quietly to spot more wildlife.

day_by_day.morning: Second zip-lining adventure at a different location if budget allows, or try a canopy walkway (hanging bridge walk) which is typically cheaper at $15-25 USD. Hanging bridges offer a different perspective of the forest canopy without the adrenaline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local coffee or chocolate farm for a budget tour ($10-20 USD). Learn about the production process and sample fresh Costa Rican coffee and cacao. A great cultural and eco-educational experience.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the resort beach. Optional: join a beach bonfire with other travelers if organized.

meals.breakfast: Tamales or empanadas from a local bakery for $2-3 USD
meals.lunch: Eat at the coffee/chocolate farm if they offer food, or pack snacks
meals.dinner: Sopa negra (black bean soup) with rice and plantains at a local soda for $5-7 USD

day_by_day.notes: Many coffee and chocolate farms offer combination tours. Buying coffee or chocolate directly from the farm is cheaper than in tourist shops and supports local farmers directly.

day_by_day.morning: Explore a different beach section or cove accessible by foot or cheap local transport. Secluded beaches often have better snorkeling and fewer crowds. Ask locals for hidden beach recommendations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Horseback riding on the beach or through the jungle with a local family-run operation ($25-40 USD for 2 hours). A classic Costa Rican eco-adventure that supports local communities.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the local town for a cultural evening. Find a live music venue, local bar, or community event. Many beachside towns have free live music on weekends.

meals.breakfast: Fruit bowl and granola from a local health food spot or market for $4-5 USD
meals.lunch: Beachside coconut rice and beans (Caribbean style if available) for $6-8 USD
meals.dinner: Grilled whole fish at a local seafood restaurant - fresh catch is affordable near the coast at $10-14 USD

day_by_day.notes: When booking horseback riding, choose family-operated farms over large commercial operators for better prices and a more authentic experience. Confirm the horses are well-treated before booking.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day eco-adventure excursion to a nearby national park or protected area. Arrive at opening time (usually 8:00 AM) to maximize wildlife sightings. Entrance fees for Costa Rican national parks are typically $18-20 USD for foreigners.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the national park. Look for wildlife on different trail systems. Bring plenty of water, sunscreen, and snacks. Hire a local guide at the park entrance for $20-30 USD to significantly enhance wildlife spotting.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. Rest and prepare for the final days of the trip. Review any souvenirs or gifts you want to purchase.

meals.breakfast: Hearty breakfast before the full day out - eggs, gallo pinto, and juice at a soda for $5-6 USD
meals.lunch: Pack lunch from the pulpería - sandwiches, fruit, nuts, and plenty of water
meals.dinner: Celebrate a great wildlife day with a slightly nicer dinner - try a local restaurant with a view for $12-16 USD

day_by_day.notes: National park trails can be muddy even in dry season. Wear waterproof hiking boots or shoes. Apply insect repellent before entering the forest. Photography is free - bring extra memory cards.

day_by_day.morning: Final wildlife morning walk at sunrise on the beach (free). This is often the best time to spot sea turtles returning from nesting, shorebirds feeding, and monkeys in the coastal trees.
day_by_day.afternoon: Souvenir shopping at local artisan markets and town shops. Buy coffee, chocolate, and handmade crafts directly from local artisans. Avoid resort gift shops which mark up prices significantly. Budget $20-40 USD for souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at your favorite local soda or restaurant discovered during the trip. Enjoy a final sunset on the beach and reflect on the trip highlights.

meals.breakfast: Special farewell breakfast - try a local café for fresh pastries, tropical fruit, and specialty Costa Rican coffee for $6-8 USD
meals.lunch: Light lunch - ceviche and patacones at a beachside spot for $7-9 USD
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at the best value local restaurant you discovered - budget $12-18 USD for a memorable final meal with a cold Imperial beer

day_by_day.notes: Pack souvenirs carefully to avoid damage. Vacuum-sealed coffee bags travel well. Check airline liquid restrictions for any bottled products. Start packing non-essentials tonight to make the final morning easier.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk on the beach (free). Take last photos and enjoy the tropical environment one final time. Check out of the resort - store luggage at reception if checkout is before departure transport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, either explore the local area one last time or head to the airport. Take the public bus or pre-booked shared shuttle to Juan Santamaría Airport. Budget $10-25 USD for shared shuttle, $3-8 USD for public bus.
day_by_day.evening: Airport departure. Arrive at least 2-3 hours before international flight. Spend remaining colones on snacks or a final coffee at the airport.

meals.breakfast: Quick and easy breakfast from the pulpería or a nearby soda - $3-5 USD
meals.lunch: Eat before reaching the airport if possible - airport food is significantly more expensive. A final casado at a local soda near the bus terminal for $6-8 USD
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport food if departure is in the evening

day_by_day.notes: Keep $25-30 USD in cash for the airport departure tax if not already included in your ticket (most modern tickets include it). Exchange remaining colones back to your home currency at the airport before departure. Keep all receipts for budget tracking.

trip_options.title: Classic Costa Rica Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits, featuring over 10 cables, Tarzan swings, and suspension bridges with breathtaking views of the forest below. A top eco-adventure experience with expert naturalist guides who point out wildlife along the way.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Wildlife Hike
experiences.description: Trek through primary rainforest on a network of hanging bridges and trails surrounding the iconic Arenal Volcano. Encounter toucans, morpho butterflies, coatis, and howler monkeys while crossing suspension bridges high above the forest floor with stunning volcano views. Guided tours include expert naturalist commentary.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked shuttle transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Scenic 2–3 hour drive through the Central Valley. Check in, freshen up, and explore the resort grounds and beachfront at leisure.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset stroll along the beach adjacent to the resort. Enjoy the Pacific coastal atmosphere and get oriented with the local area. Early night to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or grab a quick bite at the airport — Spoon café inside the terminal offers fresh Costa Rican pastries and coffee
meals.lunch: Light snack at the airport or en route — roadside 'soda' (local diner) serving casado (rice, beans, plantains, protein) for ~$8–12
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Aegean Bliss Resort restaurant — welcome meal featuring fresh grilled fish or chicken with rice and beans, $20–30 per person

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange airport shuttle in advance (~$60–90 USD). Exchange some cash to Costa Rican Colones at the airport for small purchases. Keep arrival day relaxed to adjust to the time zone.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning guided wildlife walk along the beach and mangrove estuary near the resort. Look for scarlet macaws, howler monkeys, iguanas, and shorebirds at dawn — the best time for wildlife sightings. Guided walks typically run 6:00–8:30 AM (~$25–35 per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a half-day kayaking or stand-up paddleboard (SUP) tour in the calm coastal waters near the resort. Explore hidden coves and observe marine wildlife including pelicans and sea turtles. Tours typically run 1:00–4:00 PM (~$40–55 per person).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the nearest local town on foot or by taxi. Browse artisan craft stalls and pick up souvenirs. Enjoy a relaxed dinner at a local beachside restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet — fresh tropical fruits, gallo pinto (rice and beans), eggs, and local coffee, ~$12–18
meals.lunch: Beachside casual café near the resort — fresh ceviche, patacones (fried plantains), and a cold Imperial beer or fresh fruit agua fresca, ~$10–15
meals.dinner: Local restaurant in town — whole fried snapper (pargo entero) with coconut rice and salad, ~$15–22 per person

day_by_day.notes: Apply reef-safe sunscreen and bring insect repellent for the morning wildlife walk. Wildlife activity peaks at dawn and dusk — binoculars recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to a nearby national park or wildlife refuge (such as Carara National Park if in the Central Pacific zone). Morning guided rainforest hike from 7:00–10:00 AM. Prime habitat for scarlet macaws, crocodiles along the Tárcoles River, and diverse bird species. Park entry ~$18, guided tour ~$40–55.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the national park exploration — visit the Tárcoles River Bridge for spectacular American crocodile viewing (free, roadside stop). Afternoon boat tour on the river for up-close wildlife encounters including herons, kingfishers, and crocodiles (~$35–45 per person).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by early evening. Relax at the resort pool or spa. Optional sunset yoga class on the beach if offered by the resort.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — gallo pinto, fresh fruit, and Costa Rican coffee, ~$12–18
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch packed by the resort or a local soda near the park entrance — rice and bean wraps, fresh fruit, and water, ~$8–12
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant dinner — grilled chicken or sea bass with local vegetable medley and plantains, paired with a glass of local craft beer, ~$20–28 per person

day_by_day.notes: Wear long sleeves and closed-toe shoes for the rainforest hike. Bring plenty of water and a rain jacket as afternoon showers are possible even in dry season (February). Book the river boat tour in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Depart resort early (6:00–7:00 AM) for a scenic transfer to Arenal Volcano region (~3–4 hours by shuttle, ~$40–55 per person). Arrive mid-morning and check into a mid-range eco-lodge near La Fortuna. Brief orientation walk around the town of La Fortuna.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Wildlife Hike — Trek through primary rainforest on a network of hanging bridges and trails surrounding the iconic Arenal Volcano. Spot toucans, sloths, poison dart frogs, and howler monkeys. Guided tour runs approximately 3 hours (~$35–55 per person).
day_by_day.evening: Soak in the natural hot springs heated by Arenal Volcano's geothermal activity. Mid-range hot spring parks (such as Baldi or Tabacón) offer pools and bar service (~$35–60 per person). Enjoy dinner at the hot springs complex or nearby.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at resort before departure — quick continental spread, $10–15
meals.lunch: Lunch in La Fortuna town upon arrival — local soda serving casado del día (daily set meal with protein, rice, beans, salad), ~$8–12
meals.dinner: Dinner at a La Fortuna restaurant near the hot springs — grilled tenderloin with chimichurri, yuca fries, and tropical salad, ~$18–25 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book shuttle transfers in advance through your resort or a local operator. The hanging bridges tour involves moderate walking — wear comfortable hiking shoes. Bring a swimsuit and towel for the hot springs.

day_by_day.morning: Arenal Volcano hike on the lava fields trail at Arenal Volcano National Park. Hike the Sendero Coladas (lava flow trail) for dramatic volcanic landscape views and wildlife sightings at the forest edge. Park entry ~$18, guided hike ~$35–50. Best visibility is in the morning before clouds roll in.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arenal Lake kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding with Arenal Volcano as a dramatic backdrop. Half-day tour on Lake Arenal (~$45–60 per person). Alternatively, visit the La Fortuna Waterfall — a 70-meter cascade in the jungle reached by a steep staircase trail (~$18 entry).
day_by_day.evening: Free evening in La Fortuna. Explore the town's main street, browse local shops, and enjoy a casual dinner. Optional: night wildlife walk tour (~$30–40) to spot nocturnal species including kinkajous, tree frogs, and insects.

meals.breakfast: Eco-lodge breakfast — fresh tropical fruit, eggs, gallo pinto, and local coffee, included or ~$10–14
meals.lunch: Picnic near the waterfall or lakeside café — sandwiches, fresh fruit, and cold drinks, ~$8–12
meals.dinner: La Fortuna restaurant — wood-fired pizza or traditional Costa Rican stew (olla de carne) with local craft beer, ~$14–20 per person

day_by_day.notes: The La Fortuna Waterfall stairs are steep (around 500 steps down and back up) — bring water and wear sturdy footwear. Morning hours offer the clearest views of Arenal Volcano before cloud cover builds.

day_by_day.morning: White-water rafting on the Balsa or Sarapiquí River — a thrilling Class II–III rapids experience suitable for beginners and intermediate adventurers. Full guided rafting experience with safety briefing, equipment, and transportation (~$65–85 per person). Departs 7:00–8:00 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to La Fortuna by early afternoon. Afternoon at leisure — visit the Arenal Eco Zoo or Butterfly Conservatory to observe local reptiles, amphibians, and butterfly species up close (~$15–20). Alternatively, relax at the eco-lodge pool.
day_by_day.evening: Cooking class experience with a local Costa Rican family — learn to prepare traditional dishes including gallo pinto, ceviche, and tres leches cake (~$55–75 per person). A culturally enriching and delicious evening activity.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the lodge before rafting — granola, yogurt, and fruit, ~$8–12
meals.lunch: Post-rafting lunch included with most tour packages, or local soda near the river — rice and beans with grilled chicken, ~$8–12
meals.dinner: Dishes prepared during the cooking class — a full traditional Costa Rican dinner experience included in the class fee

day_by_day.notes: Bring a change of clothes and waterproof bag for the rafting excursion. Secure all valuables at the lodge. The cooking class should be booked at least 2 days in advance through local tour operators in La Fortuna.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning birdwatching tour around Lake Arenal and the surrounding wetlands with a local expert guide. February is excellent for birding — expect to see toucans, trogons, herons, and over 50 species in a single morning (~$45–65 per person, 5:30–8:30 AM).
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from Arenal to Monteverde (~3 hours via jeep-boat-jeep combo across Lake Arenal — a scenic and iconic Costa Rican journey, ~$25–35 per person). Arrive in Monteverde, check into a mid-range cloud forest lodge, and take a short orientation walk in Santa Elena town.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Bat Jungle or Serpentarium in Santa Elena for an educational and fascinating evening wildlife encounter (~$15–20). Enjoy dinner in Santa Elena — the charming mountain town has excellent restaurant options.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast before departure — gallo pinto, eggs, fresh juice, and coffee, ~$10–14
meals.lunch: Lunch during the jeep-boat-jeep transfer — stop at a lakeside restaurant in Río Chiquito or similar village, ~$10–15
meals.dinner: Santa Elena restaurant — pasta, wood-fired pizza, or local trout dish (trucha) with cloud forest vegetables, ~$15–22 per person

day_by_day.notes: The jeep-boat-jeep transfer is the most scenic and recommended route from Arenal to Monteverde. Book it through your lodge or a local operator. Monteverde is cooler and mistier than the coast — pack a light fleece or jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour — Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. Experience 10–15 platforms, Tarzan swings, and a Superman cable over the forest canopy with breathtaking views. Tour runs approximately 3 hours (~$55–80 per person). Book with Original Canopy Tour or Sky Adventures.
day_by_day.afternoon: Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve — afternoon guided walk through one of the world's most biodiverse cloud forests. Spot resplendent quetzals (February is peak quetzal season!), three-wattled bellbirds, howler monkeys, and orchids. Entry ~$25, guided tour ~$20–30 additional.
day_by_day.evening: Night walk in the cloud forest — a magical experience spotting nocturnal wildlife including glass frogs, sleeping birds, stick insects, and kinkajous with a flashlight guide (~$25–35 per person). Return for a warm dinner.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast — fresh cloud forest honey, local cheese, gallo pinto, eggs, and coffee, ~$12–16
meals.lunch: Café near the zip-line departure point — sandwiches, empanadas, and fresh juice, ~$10–14
meals.dinner: Monteverde restaurant — hearty cloud forest fare including palmito (heart of palm) salad, grilled beef tenderloin or vegetarian casado, and local artisan cheese plate, ~$18–26 per person

day_by_day.notes: February is one of the best months to spot the resplendent quetzal in Monteverde — they are breeding during this period. Hire a guide with a spotting scope for the best quetzal viewing experience. Wear layers for the zip-line as it can be breezy and cool at canopy height.

day_by_day.morning: Curi-Cancha Wildlife Reserve — a quieter and often more rewarding alternative to the main Monteverde Reserve for wildlife viewing. Small group guided walk through primary and secondary cloud forest with excellent quetzal sightings and diverse birdlife (~$15 entry + $20–25 guided tour, 6:00–9:00 AM).
day_by_day.afternoon: Monteverde Cheese Factory (La Lechería) tour — learn about the history of the Quaker settlers who founded Monteverde and established Costa Rica's most famous artisan cheese tradition. Guided tour and tasting (~$12–18). Browse local artisan markets and coffee shops in Santa Elena.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Costa Rican music and culture show if available locally, or enjoy a relaxed evening at the lodge. Optional: visit the Children's Eternal Rain Forest viewpoint at dusk for panoramic views over the Gulf of Nicoya.

meals.breakfast: Early light snack before the morning reserve walk — granola bar and coffee from the lodge, ~$5–8
meals.lunch: Santa Elena town café — fresh Monteverde cheese quesadillas, vegetable soup, and local coffee, ~$10–14
meals.dinner: Restaurant in Santa Elena — wood-oven baked trout with cloud forest herbs, roasted yuca, and a glass of Chilean wine, ~$18–24 per person

day_by_day.notes: Curi-Cancha is less crowded than the main Monteverde Reserve and often yields better wildlife sightings. Early morning is essential for quetzal spotting. The cheese factory tour is a unique cultural experience — purchase some local cheese as a souvenir.

day_by_day.morning: Transfer from Monteverde to the Manuel Antonio / Pacific Coast area (~4–5 hours by shuttle, ~$35–50 per person). Enjoy the scenic drive through Costa Rica's diverse landscapes — from cloud forest to lowland tropics. Arrive and re-check into Aegean Bliss Resort or a nearby mid-range coastal property.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon at leisure on the beach. Swim, snorkel, or simply relax and soak in the Pacific sunshine. Optional: rent a surfboard or take a beginner surf lesson (~$35–50 including board and instructor).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dolphin-watching or sailing cruise departing from the local marina (~$55–75 per person). Watch spinner dolphins play in the bow wake and enjoy the dramatic Pacific sunset over the ocean.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast in Monteverde before departure — gallo pinto, eggs, fresh fruit, and coffee, ~$10–14
meals.lunch: Roadside stop during transfer at a local soda — casado with fresh lemonade, ~$8–12
meals.dinner: Beachfront restaurant at or near the resort — fresh grilled mahi-mahi with coconut rice, mango salsa, and a tropical cocktail, ~$20–28 per person

day_by_day.notes: Confirm shuttle transfer the evening before. The drive from Monteverde back to the Pacific coast is long but scenic — sit on the right side of the bus for the best views. Book the sunset cruise in advance as spots fill quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Manuel Antonio National Park — one of Costa Rica's most celebrated parks combining stunning beaches with extraordinary biodiversity. Morning guided hike (7:00–10:00 AM) through the park's trails to spot white-faced capuchin monkeys, two and three-toed sloths, agoutis, and hundreds of bird species. Park entry ~$20, guided tour ~$30–45.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon on Playa Manuel Antonio or Playa Biesanz — two of the most beautiful beaches inside or adjacent to the national park. Swim in the calm turquoise waters, snorkel around rocky outcrops, or simply relax under a palm tree. Bring snorkeling gear (~$10 rental).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a shower and change, then head out for a festive evening. Visit a local beachside bar for happy hour cocktails, followed by dinner at one of the area's acclaimed restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before park opening — fresh fruit, yogurt, and local coffee, ~$12–16
meals.lunch: Beach picnic or park-adjacent kiosk — fresh ceviche, fruit cups, coconut water, ~$10–15
meals.dinner: Upscale-casual restaurant with ocean view — lobster tail or whole grilled red snapper, plantain tostones, and a glass of white wine, ~$28–40 per person

day_by_day.notes: Manuel Antonio National Park has a daily visitor cap — book tickets online in advance at sinac.go.cr to guarantee entry. Monkeys in the park are habituated to humans but do NOT feed them. Keep food in sealed bags as monkeys are clever thieves.

day_by_day.morning: Horseback riding tour through the jungle and along the beach — a classic Costa Rican experience combining wildlife spotting with scenic coastal and forest landscapes (~$55–75 per person, 2–3 hours). Suitable for all experience levels. Departs 7:00–8:00 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: Catamaran snorkeling tour along the Pacific coast — sail to pristine snorkeling spots, explore coral reefs and rocky outcrops teeming with marine life including tropical fish, rays, and sea turtles (~$65–85 per person including snorkel gear, drinks, and fruit). Afternoon tour typically 1:00–5:00 PM.
day_by_day.evening: Final full evening in Costa Rica — celebrate with a special dinner at the resort's best restaurant or a highly-rated local establishment. Enjoy the ocean breeze, starry skies, and the sounds of the jungle at night.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full spread with tropical fruits, eggs to order, gallo pinto, and Costa Rican coffee, ~$12–18
meals.lunch: Lunch included on the catamaran tour — fresh fruit, sandwiches, snacks, and tropical drinks
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner — surf and turf (grilled shrimp and beef tenderloin), plantain gratin, and a bottle of wine shared between two, ~$35–50 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the catamaran snorkeling tour at least 2 days in advance. Bring biodegradable reef-safe sunscreen for snorkeling. The horseback riding tour should also be booked ahead — operators in Manuel Antonio are popular and fill up quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake up early for one last sunrise walk on the beach. Collect any remaining souvenirs from local artisan markets or shops near the resort. Pack and check out of the resort. Arrange shuttle or private transfer back to Juan Santamaría International Airport (~3–4 hours depending on departure time).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the airport with plenty of time before departure. Browse duty-free shops for last-minute Costa Rican coffee, chocolate, and artisan goods. Clear immigration and security.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Costa Rica with incredible memories of cloud forests, volcanic landscapes, zip-lines, wildlife encounters, and Pacific beaches. ¡Pura Vida!

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast or grab a quick bite at a local café — traditional gallo pinto, eggs, and the best cup of Costa Rican coffee you've had all trip, ~$10–15
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or café — light meal of arroz con pollo or a sandwich before the flight, ~$12–18
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or at layover destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your international flight for check-in, immigration, and security at SJO airport. Purchase Costa Rican coffee (Café Britt or Volcán Azul are excellent brands) and dark chocolate from duty-free as gifts. Keep a small amount of Colones for any last-minute tips or purchases.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Costa Rica Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits, featuring over 10 cables, Tarzan swings, and suspension bridges with breathtaking views of the forest below. A top eco-adventure experience with expert naturalist guides who point out wildlife along the way.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife River Safari
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle waterways of Tortuguero by canoe or small boat, spotting caimans, river turtles, howler monkeys, sloths, toucans, and vibrant poison dart frogs in their natural habitat. If visiting between July and October, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of endangered green sea turtles on the beach at night.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Wildlife Hike
experiences.description: Trek through primary rainforest on a network of hanging bridges and trails surrounding the iconic Arenal Volcano. Encounter toucans, morpho butterflies, coatis, and howler monkeys while crossing suspension bridges high above the forest floor with stunning volcano views. Guided tours include expert naturalist commentary.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Tour
experiences.description: Explore one of the world's most biodiverse national parks with a certified naturalist guide and high-powered telescope. Spot three-toed sloths, white-faced capuchin monkeys, scarlet macaws, and rare squirrel monkeys in the jungle, then relax on the park's stunning white-sand beaches framed by lush rainforest.

experiences.name: Corcovado National Park Day Trek with Naturalist Guide
experiences.description: Venture into one of the most biologically intense places on Earth, as described by National Geographic. This guided day hike through Corcovado's old-growth rainforest offers unparalleled chances to see tapirs, peccaries, scarlet macaws, poison dart frogs, and even jaguars. An unmissable bucket-list eco-adventure for serious wildlife enthusiasts.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Private airport transfer in a luxury SUV to Aegean Bliss Resort. Upon arrival, enjoy a welcome cocktail and resort orientation. Settle into your beachfront suite and take a leisurely stroll along the private beach to decompress from travel.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on your private terrace or the resort's oceanfront bar. Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at the resort's signature restaurant to acclimate and prepare for the adventures ahead.

meals.breakfast: On the plane / at the airport
meals.lunch: Light snack or airport lounge meal prior to or just after landing
meals.dinner: Signature oceanfront restaurant at Aegean Bliss Resort — fresh ceviche, grilled pargo (red snapper), and a curated Costa Rican wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Request early check-in if possible. Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel. Confirm all upcoming excursion bookings with the resort concierge this evening.

day_by_day.morning: Guided sunrise beach walk with a resort naturalist — spot shorebirds, nesting sea turtles (season-dependent), and coastal wildlife along the pristine beachfront. Follow with a full gourmet breakfast at the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Tour — explore one of the world's most biodiverse national parks with a certified naturalist guide and high-powered spotting scopes. Encounter white-faced capuchin monkeys, sloths, scarlet macaws, and agoutis along lush jungle trails leading to secluded beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a private sunset yoga session on the beach deck. Freshen up and enjoy a candlelit dinner at a premium beachside restaurant near Manuel Antonio.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet tropical breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — fresh fruit platters, eggs Benedict, Costa Rican gallo pinto, and freshly brewed local coffee
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet picnic lunch prepared by the resort, enjoyed within Manuel Antonio National Park at a scenic overlook
meals.dinner: La Luna Restaurant (Manuel Antonio area) — renowned for its ocean views and upscale Costa Rican fusion cuisine; try the sea bass in coconut sauce

day_by_day.notes: Manuel Antonio National Park has limited daily visitor quotas — book tickets well in advance. Wear light, moisture-wicking clothing and bring insect repellent. Best wildlife sightings are in the early morning hours.

day_by_day.morning: Private sport fishing charter from the marina near the resort — deep-sea fishing for marlin, sailfish, or mahi-mahi in the Pacific waters off the Central Pacific coast. Includes a private captain, first mate, and all premium tackle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to shore and head to a private catamaran cruise along the coastline — snorkel vibrant coral reefs, spot dolphins, and enjoy the dramatic Pacific coastline from the water with chilled champagne and fresh fruit.
day_by_day.evening: Beachfront bonfire arranged by the resort with a private chef preparing your catch of the day (if applicable) or a curated seafood barbecue. Stargazing session guided by the resort's astronomy concierge.

meals.breakfast: Light continental breakfast at the resort before heading to the marina — fresh pastries, tropical juices, and local coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch served aboard the catamaran — fresh ceviche, shrimp skewers, tropical fruit, and premium beverages
meals.dinner: Private beachfront bonfire dinner at the resort — grilled lobster, fresh catch of the day, plantains, and artisanal desserts

day_by_day.notes: Confirm fishing charter and catamaran cruise bookings through the resort concierge. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and light layers for the boat. Sea conditions in February are generally calm and ideal for water activities.

day_by_day.morning: Private helicopter transfer from the Central Pacific coast to the Arenal Volcano region — enjoy breathtaking aerial views of the Pacific coast, rainforest, and the iconic Arenal cone. Check into a luxury eco-lodge near Arenal for a two-night stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Wildlife Hike — trek through primary rainforest on a network of hanging bridges and elevated trails surrounding the iconic Arenal Volcano. Spot toucans, poison dart frogs, howler monkeys, and coatis with a private naturalist guide.
day_by_day.evening: Soak in private natural hot springs fed by geothermal volcanic energy at a premium hot springs resort (Tabacón Grand Spa Thermal Resort or equivalent). Enjoy a therapeutic volcanic mud treatment.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure — eggs to order, tropical fruits, local cheeses, and fresh-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Lunch at a scenic restaurant near the hanging bridges — traditional Costa Rican casado with grilled chicken or fresh fish, local lemonade
meals.dinner: Fine dining at the hot springs resort restaurant — multi-course Costa Rican tasting menu featuring local ingredients, paired with premium wines

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter transfer offers an unparalleled scenic experience and saves significant travel time vs. ground transport (approx. 4-5 hours by road). Book well in advance. The hanging bridges are accessible to moderate fitness levels. Bring waterproof layers as the Arenal area receives frequent afternoon showers.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning guided wildlife boat tour on Lake Arenal — spot kingfishers, herons, ospreys, and potentially otters along the lake shores with the dramatic Arenal Volcano as a backdrop. Bring binoculars for optimal birdwatching.
day_by_day.afternoon: White-water rafting on the Balsa River (Class II–III) — a thrilling yet accessible rafting experience through lush jungle gorges with a private guide and safety team. Suitable for all experience levels.
day_by_day.evening: Luxury spa treatment at the eco-lodge — choose from a volcanic stone massage, rainforest body wrap, or hydrotherapy session. Enjoy a private dinner under the stars at the lodge's premium restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the eco-lodge before the boat tour — granola, tropical yogurt, fresh fruits, and local coffee
meals.lunch: Riverside picnic lunch after rafting — gourmet sandwiches, fresh tropical fruit, local snacks, and cold beverages prepared by the lodge
meals.dinner: Private candlelit dinner at the Arenal eco-lodge — locally sourced ingredients featuring heart of palm salad, slow-braised beef short rib, and artisanal chocolate dessert with Arenal Volcano views

day_by_day.notes: The Balsa River rafting is best in the morning when water levels are optimal. The eco-lodge spa should be booked in advance — request the volcanic stone massage for a truly local experience. Weather around Arenal can be unpredictable; pack a quality rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Private ground transfer from Arenal to Monteverde Cloud Forest region (approximately 3 hours via scenic mountain roads or a shorter lake-and-jeep combination route). Arrive and check into a luxury cloud forest lodge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided private walk through the Santa Elena Cloud Forest Reserve — explore the mystical misty cloud forest with a certified naturalist guide. Spot resplendent quetzals (peak season Feb–April), emerald toucanets, glass frogs, and orchids.
day_by_day.evening: Twilight guided night walk through the cloud forest — discover nocturnal wildlife including kinkajous, sleeping birds, stick insects, and tree frogs with a specialized night-tour guide using red-light torches.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the Arenal eco-lodge before departure — traditional gallo pinto, fresh eggs, tropical fruits, and Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a charming café in the Monteverde village upon arrival — homemade cheese (Monteverde is famous for its dairy), fresh bread, and local soups
meals.dinner: Fine dining at the cloud forest lodge — farm-to-table Costa Rican cuisine featuring locally produced cheese, vegetables from the lodge garden, and premium Costa Rican craft beer or wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: February is one of the best months to spot the resplendent quetzal in Monteverde during breeding season — a bucket-list wildlife sighting. The jeep-boat-jeep transfer from Arenal to Monteverde (via Lake Arenal) is scenic and faster than the road route. Pack warm layers as Monteverde can be cool and misty.

day_by_day.morning: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour — soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. Experience multiple cables, Tarzan swings, and suspension bridges with panoramic cloud forest views. Private group booking for an exclusive experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monteverde Butterfly Garden and Hummingbird Gallery — explore enclosed tropical gardens teeming with hundreds of butterfly species and dozens of hummingbird species feeding at close range. Follow with a guided visit to a local coffee and chocolate farm for a premium tasting experience.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private traditional Costa Rican cooking class with a local chef at the lodge — learn to prepare authentic dishes using local ingredients. Enjoy the meal you've prepared with premium local wines.

meals.breakfast: Hearty breakfast at the cloud forest lodge before the zip-line tour — energy-rich options including eggs, whole-grain toast, fresh tropical fruits, and strong Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Artisanal lunch at the coffee and chocolate farm — farm-fresh salads, handmade tortillas, local cheeses, and specialty pour-over coffee
meals.dinner: Your own creations from the private cooking class — traditional Costa Rican dishes such as olla de carne, plantain dishes, and tres leches cake, paired with local wines

day_by_day.notes: The zip-line tour should be booked for the morning when mist is lighter and visibility is better. Wear closed-toe shoes and comfortable clothing. The Monteverde coffee and chocolate tasting is a premium cultural experience not to be missed — look for single-origin dark chocolate tastings.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning birdwatching walk with a specialist ornithologist guide in the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve — one of the most biodiverse cloud forests on Earth. Target species include the resplendent quetzal, three-wattled bellbird, and bare-necked umbrellabird.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private ground transfer from Monteverde to Tortuguero on the Caribbean coast (via San José, approximately 5–6 hours, or arrange a private charter flight for efficiency). Check into a premium eco-lodge within or adjacent to Tortuguero National Park.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome briefing with your Tortuguero naturalist guide. Enjoy a relaxing dinner at the lodge overlooking the jungle canals. Listen to the symphony of tropical frogs and insects as night falls over the Caribbean rainforest.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the Monteverde lodge before the birdwatching walk — fresh fruits, yogurt, granola, and local coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch en route during the transfer — stop at a quality restaurant in the Central Valley highlands near San José for traditional Costa Rican cuisine
meals.dinner: Caribbean-inspired dinner at the Tortuguero eco-lodge — rice and beans cooked in coconut milk, fresh Caribbean lobster, and plantain dishes with tropical fruit desserts

day_by_day.notes: A private charter flight from Monteverde/San José to Tortuguero is highly recommended to avoid the long road and boat transfer — it reduces travel time from 5+ hours to approximately 45 minutes. Tortuguero is only accessible by air or boat, adding to its remote, pristine character.

day_by_day.morning: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife River Safari — glide through the jungle waterways of Tortuguero by private canoe and small motorized boat, spotting caimans, river turtles, Jesus Christ lizards, river otters, manatees (if lucky), and an extraordinary array of tropical birds including kingfishers, anhingas, and toucans.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided hike through the rainforest trails of Tortuguero National Park with your private naturalist guide — explore the dense jungle interior, learn about medicinal plants, and spot howler monkeys, sloths, and poison dart frogs.
day_by_day.evening: Sea turtle nesting beach walk (February is early season — check current nesting activity with the lodge). If turtles are active, a licensed guide will lead a respectful, low-impact viewing experience. Return to the lodge for a Caribbean dinner and evening drinks.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the eco-lodge before the early morning safari — traditional Caribbean-style breakfast with eggs, rice and beans, fresh tropical fruits, and local coffee
meals.lunch: Fresh lunch at the lodge after the morning safari — Caribbean fish stew, patacones (fried plantains), fresh salads, and tropical fruit juices
meals.dinner: Premium dinner at the lodge's restaurant — whole grilled Caribbean snapper, coconut curry prawns, and a curated rum cocktail tasting featuring premium Caribbean and Costa Rican rums

day_by_day.notes: The morning wildlife safari should begin at dawn (around 5:30–6:00 AM) for optimal wildlife activity. Bring waterproof bags for cameras and electronics as the canoe tour may involve some spray. February is the beginning of the green turtle nesting season — confirm current activity with lodge staff.

day_by_day.morning: Private charter flight from Tortuguero to Puerto Jiménez (Osa Peninsula) — aerial views of the Caribbean coast, Central Valley, and Pacific lowlands. Check into a luxury eco-lodge near Corcovado National Park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Orientation walk around the lodge's private reserve with a resident naturalist — spot scarlet macaws (abundant in the Osa), white-lipped peccaries, and tapir tracks. Visit a local sustainable cacao farm for a bean-to-bar chocolate experience.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset kayaking through the mangroves of the Golfo Dulce — spot roosting scarlet macaws, herons, and bioluminescent plankton (conditions permitting) as dusk falls. Return to the lodge for a premium dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the Tortuguero lodge before departure — fresh fruits, pastries, and local coffee
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch at the Osa Peninsula eco-lodge upon arrival — fresh ceviche, tropical salads, and artisanal lemonade
meals.dinner: Gourmet dinner at the lodge — locally sourced ingredients featuring heart of palm soup, grilled pargo with mango salsa, and a locally made artisanal chocolate dessert platter

day_by_day.notes: The Osa Peninsula is one of the most remote and biodiverse regions in Costa Rica. The private charter flight is essential as ground access is extremely limited. Confirm lodge transfer from the airstrip in advance. The bioluminescence kayaking is weather and tide dependent — ask the lodge for the best timing.

day_by_day.morning: Corcovado National Park Day Trek with Naturalist Guide — venture into one of the most biologically intense places on Earth (as described by National Geographic) via the La Leona or San Pedrillo entrance. Trek through pristine primary rainforest with a certified naturalist, spotting Baird's tapirs, giant anteaters, pumas (tracks), four species of monkeys, and an extraordinary diversity of birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Corcovado exploration — visit pristine jungle-backed beaches within the park, snorkel in crystal-clear tide pools, and enjoy a gourmet packed lunch in a remote jungle clearing. Return to the lodge by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Private yoga and meditation session at the lodge's open-air jungle platform as howler monkeys call in the canopy above. Followed by a premium spa treatment — choose from a jungle botanical massage or rainforest aromatherapy treatment.

meals.breakfast: Early hearty breakfast at the lodge before the full-day trek — eggs, gallo pinto, fresh tropical fruits, whole-grain toast, and strong local coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch prepared by the lodge's chef, enjoyed in Corcovado — artisanal sandwiches, fresh fruit, energy bars, and cold beverages
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at the eco-lodge — multi-course tasting menu featuring Osa Peninsula local specialties: pejibaye palm soup, fresh jungle heart-of-palm salad, grilled local fish, and artisanal chocolate truffles

day_by_day.notes: Corcovado requires advance permits (limited daily visitor numbers) — the lodge concierge must arrange these well in advance. Wear sturdy waterproof hiking boots, long pants, and apply insect repellent. The trek involves river crossings and can be strenuous — a moderate-to-good fitness level is recommended. This is arguably the most spectacular wildlife day of the entire trip.

day_by_day.morning: Private dolphin and whale watching boat tour in the Golfo Dulce — one of only two tropical fjords in the world, home to resident bottlenose and spinner dolphins, humpback whales (migration season), and whale sharks. Snorkel in pristine coral gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Osa Peninsula lodge for a private wellness afternoon — enjoy the infinity pool overlooking the jungle, a hammock session in the private reserve, and a personal mixology class with a local bartender crafting premium tropical cocktails using local fruits and premium spirits.
day_by_day.evening: Private farewell dinner on a secluded jungle beach — the lodge arranges a torchlit table directly on the sand with a personal chef preparing a curated seafood feast. Toast to an extraordinary journey through Costa Rica's most spectacular ecosystems.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the lodge — smoothie bowls, eggs Benedict with local cheese, fresh tropical fruits, and specialty Costa Rican pour-over coffee
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch served aboard the boat — ceviche, shrimp cocktail, fresh fruit, and chilled beverages
meals.dinner: Private torchlit beach dinner — whole grilled lobster, ceviche trio, coconut-glazed prawns, plantain dessert, and premium champagne

day_by_day.notes: February is an excellent month for dolphin sightings in the Golfo Dulce. Humpback whale sightings are possible as Southern Hemisphere humpbacks sometimes appear in early February. Confirm the private beach dinner setup with the lodge concierge at least 48 hours in advance. This is a truly memorable final evening experience.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk through the lodge's private reserve with a naturalist guide — a quiet, reflective farewell to the extraordinary biodiversity of the Osa Peninsula. Spot early morning birds, listen to howler monkeys, and capture final photographs of the jungle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private charter flight from Puerto Jiménez to San José (Juan Santamaría International Airport) — approximately 45 minutes. Arrive with ample time for international departure formalities. Enjoy a final Costa Rican coffee and souvenir shopping at the airport's premium duty-free shops.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry the memories of 13 extraordinary days exploring Costa Rica's most iconic ecosystems, from Pacific beaches to cloud forests, volcanic landscapes, Caribbean jungles, and the wild Osa Peninsula.

meals.breakfast: Final full breakfast at the Osa eco-lodge — a celebratory spread of all your favorite Costa Rican dishes from the trip, fresh tropical fruits, and the finest local coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the San José airport — premium airport lounge dining or a quality restaurant in the terminal
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the private charter flight from Puerto Jiménez to San José well in advance and confirm the exact timing based on your international departure flight. Allow a minimum of 3 hours between the charter arrival and international departure. Consider purchasing premium Costa Rican coffee, artisanal chocolate, and locally made souvenirs at the airport. A tip envelope for all guides and lodge staff is a thoughtful and appreciated gesture.
